constraint_decided_it: E74's scope note explicitly extends Group to 'official positions which used to be regarded in certain contexts as one actor, independent of the current holder of the office ... it may happen that the group never had more than one member'; E85's scope note names 'the inauguration of somebody into an official position' and E86's names 'the end of tenure of somebody in an official position', and P146's own example is 'George Washington's leaving office in 1797 (E86) separated from the office of President of the United States (E74)'. B rejects E85/E86 on the ground that 'there is no group here', which is precisely the case E74 was extended to cover, and B's fallback E30/P75 is blocked by E30 ('legal privileges') and P75 ('over which the actor holds or has held a legal claim') for a right the case states is customary and non-legal.
better_modelling: The prescribed base-CRM modelling is A's: one E74 Group standing for the office 'fire-keeper of the midsummer bonfire' (singleton office reading, sanctioned by E74's scope note and by the SIG's own 2008 negative vote on P107.1 in t0431, 'following our definition of Group, it can be also an office or position ... this could consistently describe changing positions'); each succession as an E85 Joining (P143 incoming person, P144 the office) plus an E86 Leaving (P145 outgoing person, P146 the office), each with its own E52 Time-Span via P4 and fuzzy boundaries via P81a/b and P82a/b; P107 has current or former member as the shortcut for the chain. Where A also errs by omission: P144.1 / P107.1 kind of member is a live construct in v7.3.2 and is the declared way to type the role, so it is available and A should not have discarded it. The E30/P75 layer B builds on should be dropped or heavily caveated, since E30 is scoped to legal privileges.
reasoning: A applies E85/E86 within their declared domain and range (P143 E85->E39, P144 E85->E74, P145 E86->E39, P146 E86->E74) against an E74 office, which is the exact pattern E74/E85/E86 scope notes and P146's George Washington example prescribe; its informality argument also holds, since P12's necessity is discharged automatically by P143/P145, which are subproperties of P11, itself a subproperty of P12, so no third-party witness is required. A is nevertheless marked unsupported, not correct, because its third rejected alternative asserts that P144.1/P107.1 'does not appear in the current v7.3.2 property list via docs search' when both P144 and P107's v7.3.2 declarations carry the kind-of-member scope-note sentence and the FOL clauses P144(x,y,z) and P107(x,y,z); its other citations (t0873's 1754 club election with fuzzy P81/P82, t1806's butler case and 'CRMbase does not offer other constructs', the Objectives passage counting oral tradition as evidence) do check out. B is wrong on the modelling: it discards E85/E86 on a premise E74's scope note directly contradicts, asserts E30/P75 is 'exactly what E30/P75 exist for' when both are scoped to legal privileges and legal claims, and misreads P12 as demanding witnesses in order to prefer E4 Period, which models no transfer at all; its issue chain (172/335/421/408) and the t0507 quote 'I don't like that solution' are all accurately cited, but accurate negative evidence about CRMsoc does not license ignoring the base-CRM construct that already covers office succession.
